title: Grade 9 Science — Structure of the Atom
description: Sub-atomic particles, atomic models, electronic configuration
subject: science

questions.question: Who proposed the nuclear model of the atom (planetary model)?
questions.explanation: Ernest Rutherford proposed the nuclear model (1911) based on his gold foil experiment. He showed that atoms have a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus surrounded by electrons.

questions.question: In Rutherford's gold foil experiment, most alpha particles passed straight through because:
options: Atoms are mostly empty space; the nucleus is tiny
Gold is a very thin metal
questions.explanation: Most alpha particles passed through because atoms are mostly empty space. Only a few were deflected (hit the tiny nucleus). This showed the nucleus is very small but very dense and positively charged.

questions.question: J.J. Thomson discovered the:
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron (1897) using cathode ray tube experiments. He proposed the 'plum pudding model' — electrons embedded in a positive sphere.

questions.question: The atomic number of an element equals the number of:
options: Protons in the nucleus (= electrons in a neutral atom)
questions.explanation: Atomic number (Z) = number of protons = number of electrons (in a neutral atom). It uniquely identifies an element. Mass number (A) = protons + neutrons.

questions.question: The mass number (A) of an atom is:
options: Number of protons + number of neutrons
questions.explanation: Mass number (A) = number of protons (Z) + number of neutrons (N). A = Z + N. E.g., Carbon-12: 6 protons + 6 neutrons = mass number 12.

questions.question: Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have:
options: Same number of protons and neutrons
Same number of protons but different number of neutrons
Different number of protons but same neutrons
Same atomic mass but different atomic number
questions.explanation: Isotopes: same element (same atomic number Z = same protons), but different mass numbers (different number of neutrons). E.g., Carbon-12 (6n) and Carbon-14 (8n) — both have 6 protons.

questions.question: The maximum number of electrons in the first shell (K shell) is:
questions.explanation: Maximum electrons in shells: K(n=1) = 2, L(n=2) = 8, M(n=3) = 18, N(n=4) = 32. Formula: 2n². For n=1: 2×1² = 2.

questions.question: What is the electronic configuration of sodium (atomic number 11)?
questions.explanation: Sodium (Na) has 11 electrons. Fill shells: K=2, L=8, M=1. Configuration: 2, 8, 1. The 1 electron in the outermost shell explains sodium's high reactivity.

questions.question: Valency of an element is defined as the:
options: Number of electrons in the atom
Number of electrons in the outermost shell
Combining capacity of an atom (number of electrons gained, lost, or shared)
questions.explanation: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom — how many electrons it gains, loses, or shares to achieve a stable electronic configuration (like a noble gas). It determines how atoms bond.

questions.question: Bohr's model of the atom proposed that electrons:
options: Are randomly distributed around the nucleus
Move in specific fixed orbits (shells) without losing energy
questions.explanation: Bohr's model (1913): electrons revolve around the nucleus in specific fixed circular orbits (called shells or energy levels). In these orbits they don't emit radiation — a key improvement over Rutherford's model.

questions.question: An atom of chlorine has atomic number 17. How many electrons are in its outermost shell?
questions.explanation: Cl (17 electrons): K=2, L=8, M=7. Outermost shell (M) has 7 electrons. This is why chlorine needs 1 more electron to complete its octet — it is highly reactive and forms Cl⁻ ion.

questions.question: Isobars are atoms that have:
options: Same atomic number but different mass numbers
Same mass number but different atomic numbers (different elements)
questions.explanation: Isobars: same mass number (A), different atomic numbers (Z). E.g., Ca (Z=20, A=40) and Ar (Z=18, A=40) — both have mass number 40 but are different elements.

questions.question: Who discovered the neutron?
questions.explanation: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932. He bombarded beryllium with alpha particles and detected a neutral particle with mass similar to the proton.

questions.question: The charge and mass of an electron are approximately:
questions.explanation: Electron: charge = −1 (−1.6×10⁻¹⁹ coulombs), mass = 9.1×10⁻³¹ kg ≈ 1/1836 of a proton mass (negligible). Proton: +1 charge, 1 amu. Neutron: 0 charge, 1 amu.

questions.question: The number of neutrons in Carbon-14 (atomic number 6) is:
questions.explanation: Neutrons = Mass number − Atomic number = 14 − 6 = 8. Carbon-14 has 6 protons and 8 neutrons. It is a radioactive isotope used in carbon dating.
